extracted.intended_audience: researchers, funding-agency staff, and early-career grant applicants interested in grant peer review
extracted.subtask_description: A systematic synthesis of empirical studies identifying the evaluation criteria peers use to assess grant applications; maps criteria to evaluated entities and proposes a conceptualization (aims, means, outcomes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion evaluates an entity in terms of general quality (incl. quality, poor – good, weak – strong).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'methodological quality', 'weak dissemination plan'. Occurred in the studies (full counting N=387) and used to assess entities in more general terms (e.g., method in general). Used with project and applicant. Part of the research-quality group (with appropriateness, rigor, coherence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion evaluates the originality of an entity. Indicated by adjectives such as new, novel, original, innovative, unusual, unconventional, or derivations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'originality of the study', 'new theory'. Most ubiquitous criterion — appeared in all included studies. Used primarily to assess the project's aims and outcomes (research question, topic, results).

rubrics_metrics.name: General relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion evaluates the relevance of an entity without specifying for whom or what the entity is of value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicated by nouns like significance, relevance, importance, usefulness, timeliness. Example: 'significance of the proposal’s focus'. Rare relative to domain-specific relevance criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion evaluates the relevance of an entity for academia (e.g. significance for the scientific community, a research field, for scientific/theoretical advances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'significance of the scientific investigation within its own field', 'significance of impact on academia'. Appeared in multiple studies (8 studies). Used mainly to assess aims and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extra-academic relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion evaluates the relevance of an entity for the non-academic sphere (e.g. for society, policy, economy, technology, education, health care).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'the research has practical relevance for health promotion activities'. One of the most frequent criteria (14% of assigned codes). Used mainly to judge aims and outcomes (societal impact).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion evaluates the appropriateness of an entity. Indicated by adjectives such as appropriate, adequate, sufficient, suitable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'appropriateness of the funds requested', 'inappropriate protection of human subjects'. Frequently used and, with completeness and coherence, applied to many sub-entities (used across project, applicant, environment). One of the criteria used to assess research process entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion evaluates whether/how an entity has been, is or will be done according to scholarly standards for conducting research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicated by verbs (done, measured, pre-registered), adjectives (sound, rigorous), or related nouns. Examples: 'the approach is sound', 'the evaluation plan is rigorous.' Used mainly for research-process entities (data, methods, analysis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherence/justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion evaluates the coherence of one or several entities or whether an entity is justified. Indicated by adjectives such as aligned, coherent, consistent, justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'there is coherence between the research problems, research question(s) and research methodology', 'analytic plan lacks justification'. Used mainly to assess research-process entities and often paired with rigor and appropriateness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion evaluates whether an entity is (completely) described or reported. Indicated by verbs such as addressed, articulated, described, defined, detailed, specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'All key elements of the research are defined.', 'The evaluation plan is described in the proposal.' One of the most frequent criteria (13% of assigned codes). Used with both project and applicant; contributes to the 'quality of description' dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion evaluates an entity with regard to its comprehensibility and clarity. Indicated by adjectives such as clear, comprehensible, explicit, organized, well written.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'clear presentation (interview)', 'application poorly written and/or disorganized'. Frequent (10% of assigned codes). Used for descriptive quality of proposals (how well information is presented).

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion evaluates the feasibility of an entity. Indicated by adjectives such as capable, feasible, practical, realistic, viable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Verifiable qualifications and evidence of data access demonstrate that the applicants are capable of carrying out the project.' One of the top criteria (10% of codes) and was used across applicant, project, and environment; used to assess resources, plan, applicant abilities (instrumental role).

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion evaluates an entity in terms of diversity and heterogeneity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'institutional diversity', 'disciplinary diversity', 'cultural diversity among the organization's staff and board'. Appears in analyses of applicant/person-level considerations and features in a community focused on person/sociological assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motivation
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion evaluates the motivation of an applicant. Indicated by nouns such as ambition, determination, perseverance, or willingness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'enthusiasm of the applicant'. Appeared rarely and (in the included studies) was used exclusively to evaluate the applicant (person-level criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Traits
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion evaluates an applicant along personality or trait dimensions (authenticity, humility, intelligence, independence, talent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'humility'. Rare in the included studies and used exclusively for applicant/person assessments; grouped with motivation and diversity in a small, distinct community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other (residual)
rubrics_metrics.description: Residual category containing criteria that could not be assigned to any of the other evaluation criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Letters of support are lacking.' Used to capture additional or unspecified evaluative comments; indicates the taxonomy is not exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic importance (funding-agency criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion emphasized by funding agencies concerning the strategic importance of a proposal (e.g., alignment with agency priorities or strategic goals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentioned as part of prescriptive funder criteria that differ from peer criteria; not prominent in peer-review repertoires analyzed. Examples reported in Berning et al. (2015).

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion of public understanding of science (funding-agency criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion that evaluates a proposal's potential to promote public understanding or engagement with science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified among agency criteria (Abdoul et al. 2012) and not typically part of peers' implicit repertoires in the synthesized studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental sustainability (funding-agency criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion that evaluates environmental sustainability aspects of proposed work, as emphasized by some funders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentioned as an example of funder-prescribed criteria (Langfeldt and Scordato 2016) which peers in the synthesized studies did not generally include.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return on investment (funding-agency criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion concerning expected economic or societal return on the funding invested in the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentioned as a funder criterion (Falk-Krzesinski and Tobin 2015); differs from peers' repertoires and reflects funders' boundary role between research and policy domains.
